title: Applied anatomy: the larynx and emergency front-of-neck airway

guidelineVersions: Difficult Airway Society guidelines (2025, Br J Anaesth 2026)

brief.role: Core surgical trainee in the emergency department
brief.scenario: Euan Fraser, 38, has severe facial injuries. Intubation has failed, a supraglottic airway and facemask cannot oxygenate him, and his saturations are falling.
brief.task: Answer the examiner's questions on the anatomy of the larynx and relate them to emergency front-of-neck access.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Cartilages, nerves, the membrane, then declare and perform the front-of-neck airway.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Describing anatomy while nobody has declared 'cannot intubate, cannot oxygenate'.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "This is cannot intubate, cannot oxygenate: he needs a front-of-neck airway now."

grid.label: Cartilages and membranes
grid.fail: Cannot name the thyroid and cricoid cartilages.
grid.pass: Thyroid, cricoid and epiglottis; paired arytenoid, corniculate and cuneiform; thyrohyoid and cricothyroid membranes.
grid.high: Cricoid is the only complete ring; vocal folds lie at the level of the thyroid cartilage, so the membrane is below the cords.

grid.label: Nerves and vessels
grid.fail: Cannot name the nerve supply of the larynx.
grid.pass: Cricothyroid: external laryngeal nerve. Other intrinsic muscles: recurrent laryngeal. Sensation above the cords internal laryngeal, below recurrent.
grid.high: Superior and inferior laryngeal arteries from the superior and inferior thyroid arteries.

grid.label: Find the membrane
grid.fail: Places the membrane at the thyroid notch or below the cricoid.
grid.pass: Midline, between thyroid cartilage above and cricoid below, found with the neck fully extended.
grid.high: The cricothyroid artery crosses the upper half, so the cut is in the lower half; the membrane is about 10 mm high.

grid.label: Declare the emergency
grid.fail: Keeps trying to intubate as saturations fall.
grid.pass: Declares 'cannot intubate, cannot oxygenate' once Plans A to C fail; calls for help; full-dose neuromuscular blocker; oxygen from above.
grid.high: Membrane palpability should be stated by the end of Plan A; pillow under the shoulders for maximal extension.

grid.label: Scalpel-bougie-tube
grid.fail: Proposes a needle and cannot describe a scalpel technique.
grid.pass: Number 10 blade transverse stab through membrane, turn 90° edge caudal, bougie down the blade, 6.0 cuffed tube, capnography.
grid.high: If impalpable or uncertain: vertical midline skin incision up to 8 cm, caudad to cephalad, blunt dissection, then the transverse stab.

grid.label: Limits and aftercare
grid.fail: Cannot name a complication or when to avoid the technique.
grid.pass: Bleeding, false passage, posterior tracheal or oesophageal injury, later subglottic stenosis. Adult guideline: children follow paediatric guidance.
grid.high: Laryngeal fracture or tracheal transection needs access below the injury; secure the tube, chest X-ray, senior surgical airway review.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Name the cartilages of the larynx.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: The hyoid and the trachea, I think.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: The vagus, I'm not sure which branch.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Where on the neck would you go in, and how would you find it?

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: How would you get an airway through the neck?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I'd put a needle in and jet ventilate.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Not really, it's a small cut.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Name the cartilages and membranes of the larynx.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Thyroid cartilage, cricoid below, epiglottis above. Paired arytenoids, corniculates and cuneiforms. Thyrohyoid membrane above, cricothyroid membrane between thyroid and cricoid.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Cricothyroid is the external laryngeal nerve; all other intrinsic muscles, the recurrent laryngeal. Sensation above the cords is internal laryngeal, below is recurrent.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Where on the neck would you go in, and how would you find it?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: In the midline, with the neck extended, between the thyroid cartilage and the cricoid ring.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: This is cannot intubate, cannot oxygenate. I'd call for help, ensure full paralysis, keep oxygen going from above and do a front-of-neck airway.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Scalpel-bougie-tube. Number 10 blade, transverse stab through the membrane, turn it 90 degrees edge towards the feet, bougie down the blade, 6.0 cuffed tube, inflate and confirm with capnography.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Bleeding, false passage, injury to the back wall of the trachea or oesophagus, and later subglottic stenosis. The guideline is for adults; children follow paediatric guidance.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: The cricoid is the only complete ring. The cords sit at the level of the thyroid cartilage, so the membrane is below them.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Superior and inferior laryngeal arteries, from the superior and inferior thyroid arteries.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: In the lower half. The membrane is only about 10 mm high and the cricothyroid artery crosses its upper half.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: When should you have thought about this?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Palpability should be stated by the end of Plan A. I'd put a pillow under his shoulders for maximal extension.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: You can't feel the membrane: his neck is swollen.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Vertical midline skin incision up to 8 cm, bottom to top, blunt dissection with my fingers to find it, then the transverse stab, bougie and tube.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: A laryngeal fracture: I'd go below the injury. Afterwards, secure the tube, chest X-ray, and a senior surgical airway review.

failures.move: Repeating intubation attempts as saturations fall.
failures.consequence: Hypoxic brain injury or cardiac arrest while the neck stays untouched.

failures.move: Choosing a needle and jet ventilation.
failures.consequence: Current DAS guidance sets out a scalpel-bougie-tube technique for Plan D.

failures.move: Cutting below the cricoid or at the thyroid notch.
failures.consequence: Misses the membrane; risks thyroid bleeding or the cords.
No plan to confirm placement or manage a false passage.

recovery.line: Cannot intubate, cannot oxygenate: scalpel, bougie, tube.
Vertical midline skin incision, then find the membrane with my fingers.

knowledge.fact: Cricothyroid: external laryngeal nerve; other intrinsic muscles: recurrent laryngeal.
Membrane about 10 mm high; cricothyroid artery crosses its upper half.
Scalpel-bougie-tube: number 10 blade, bougie, 6.0 cuffed tube; confirm with waveform capnography.
Uncertain palpability: vertical skin incision up to 8 cm as default.

recall.trap: More intubation attempts while oxygen falls.
recall.finish: Secure, confirm, chest X-ray, surgical airway review.

sources.name: Ahmad I, El-Boghdadly K, Iliff H, et al. Difficult Airway Society 2025 guidelines for management of unanticipated difficult tracheal intubation in adults. Br J Anaesth 2026;136:283–307
sources.supports: Plan D after failure of Plans A–C in a 'cannot intubate, cannot oxygenate' scenario; full-dose neuromuscular blockade; maximal neck extension; number 10 blade, bougie and 6.0 cuffed tube; transverse stab and 90° turn; vertical incision up to 8 cm as default when palpability is uncertain; waveform capnography; oxygen from above

sources.name: Dover K, Howdieshell TR, Colborn GL. The dimensions and vascular anatomy of the cricothyroid membrane: relevance to emergent surgical airway access. Clin Anat 1996;9:291–5
sources.supports: Membrane height about 10 mm; cricothyroid artery crosses the upper half of the membrane

partner.opening: Name the cartilages and membranes of the larynx, from the hyoid down to the trachea.

reveals.finding: SpO2 70% and falling. No end-tidal CO2 trace with facemask or supraglottic airway.
Neck swollen; membrane not clearly palpable.

reveals.trigger: Candidate asks how placement is confirmed
reveals.finding: Sustained capnography trace after tube placement.

push.question: Where would you cut, and why there?
push.expect: Lower half of the membrane; artery crosses the upper half.

push.question: What if you can't feel the membrane?
push.expect: Vertical midline skin incision up to 8 cm, blunt dissection.

curveballs.prompt: Should you wake him up instead?
curveballs.safeAnswer: Not with falling saturations and no oxygenation: front-of-neck airway now.
Adult guideline does not apply; follow paediatric guidance and get senior help.

curveballs.prompt: No capnography trace after the tube.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Assume it is not in the trachea; call for senior help and re-site it.
